st.headline: Bitcoin slides as Democratic sweep bets threaten crypto agenda
st.teaser: The original cryptocurrency slid as much as 2.8% to 75,630.57 in Asia trading on Nov 4.
fullText: WASHINGTON – Bitcoin fell to a seven-week low as the prospect of a Democratic sweep of the US Congress began showing up in early US midterm election results, adding political uncertainty to a market already struggling with fragile investor appetite.
The original cryptocurrency slid as much as 2.8% to 75,630.57 in Asia trading on Nov 4 , its lowest level since Sept 17.
It pared some losses to trade around US$76,600 (S$98,000) as of 12.20pm in Singapore.
The move followed declines in US stock futures and the dollar , while Treasuries gained, reflecting expectations that Democratic control of Congress could lead to gridlock in Washington.

“Markets react to change, and a blue flip will likely introduce additional scepticism given the party’s historically choke-point stance toward crypto,” said Daniel Reis-Faria, chief executive officer of ZeroStack. “I expect that uncertainty to be temporary.”
Major cryptocurrencies began sliding as initial vote counts came in.
Democrats, who have traditionally favoured tighter oversight of the crypto industry, had been expected to take control of the House of Representatives, a result that is now projected.
They are also projected to take control of the US Senate.
The digital-asset industry has poured money into shaping the political landscape since Trump ran for a second presidential term in 2024.

Crypto companies contributed US$189 million to political action committees in the 2026 midterm cycle through the first quarter – more than a third of election spending, according to the consumer rights advocacy group Public Citizen.
For investors, the immediate concern is that a Democratic takeover could stall industry-backed legislation and bring tougher scrutiny of digital-asset firms.
The broader macroeconomic implications are less clear.
Political stalemate could limit further fiscal stimulus and weigh on speculative assets, though lower Treasury yields could eventually provide support by easing financial conditions.
For now, Bitcoin trading offers limited utility as a gauge of broader market sentiment.
Crypto has been grappling with the fallout from a US$6.3 billion hack of largest exchange Binance last week and diminished retail enthusiasm amid the artificial intelligence boom.
Those pressures make it harder to separate the macro-driven market moves from industry-specific issues already weighing on digital assets.
“Overall sentiment in crypto is near-term moderate fear and long-term uncertainty,” said Damien Loh, chief investment officer at Ericsenz Capital.
“Near-term fear because it is still tracking overall risk assets, and with the tech selloff and potentially a restart to the war in the Middle East that is causing some downward pressure.”
Democratic control of the Senate, in addition to the House, would put Congress at odds with US President Donald Trump’s Republican White House.
The Trump family’s financial gains from its crypto ventures became a contentious issue in 2026 , helping derail a regulatory bill seen as critical to the industry.

“With the Clarity Act already stalled in the Senate, a change in committee control would most likely mean renegotiation rather than a quick revival, and markets had largely priced that in,” said Rachael Lucas, an analyst at BTC Markets.
Bitcoin is down roughly 6% from the high on Oct 29 , before the Binance hack.
More than US$1 billion flowed out of US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds on Oct 30 and Nov 2 .
Options markets continued to show demand for downside protection across maturities, even as open interest remains tilted toward calls, or the right to buy Bitcoin, in several of the largest expiries.
“As a Democratic sweep became more likely, clients shifted from buying upside calls to downside puts,” said Sean McNulty, a derivatives trader at market maker AQC Tech.
“Attention is shifting back to interest rates and currencies, which is also driving Bitcoin’s decline today.” BLOOMBERG

cna.headline: Indonesian ex-police chief may have committed 'treason' by wiretapping president: Government
cna.teaser: Listyo Sigit Prabowo had served as the national police chief during the period of the alleged wiretapping.
fullText: JAKARTA: Indonesia's former police chief, fired this week from his latest post as presidential chief of staff, may have committed "treason" through his alleged involvement in wiretapping the head of state's telephone , the government said on Wednesday (Nov 4).

"What was done may have fallen into the category of being considered as leading to treason," presidential spokesman Prasetyo Hadi told reporters in Jakarta of Tuesday's arrest of Listyo Sigit Prabowo.
"This also constitutes actions that endanger the security of the interests of the state, including jeopardising the safety of the country’s leader," he said.

On Tuesday, the national police announced it had arrested Listyo and two other senior officers for allegedly tapping the phone of President Prabowo Subianto, government officials and politicians, journalists, NGO representatives and businesspeople.
Prabowo, who took office in 2024, has come under increasing pressure for his government's handling of the economy and destructive wildfires in the Southeast Asian archipelago.
The former general reshuffled his Cabinet for a seventh time last month, appointing Listyo, 57, as his chief of staff.
Listyo had until then served as national police chief during the period of the alleged wiretapping that investigators said started in 2025.
On Wednesday, Prasetyo said the reason for the wiretap was not yet known.

"When we talk about the head of state ... there is a great deal of information there that is naturally very sensitive, which could endanger ... the interests and the strength of the nation and the state," he said.
Prasetyo added the president had expressed his "profound concern" about the case.
